description: The National Wastewater Surveillance System (NWSS) is the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's programme for tracking pathogens in sewage, and its public SARS-CoV-2 data are published on data.cdc.gov. The current dataset, CDC Wastewater Data for SARS-CoV-2 (created July 2025), holds about 619,000 rows, one per sample collection day at an anonymised sampling site, with 38 columns covering jurisdiction, county, collection date, concentration and derived metrics. Rows come from state and local health departments funded through the ELC cooperative agreement, from CDC's national testing contract (currently Verily) and from WastewaterSCAN. It is refreshed weekly and is public domain, except that WastewaterSCAN rows carry Stanford's CC BY-NC 4.0 terms. The earlier NWSS Public SARS-CoV-2 Wastewater Metric Data (837,000 rows, one per site and 15-day window) was archived on 12 September 2025. Caveats: laboratories, methods and sampling frequency differ between sites, so CDC advises against comparing concentrations across locations; site identities are anonymised to arbitrary integers; and the cdc.gov programme pages refused access from the cataloguing session. Simulation uses: an operational wastewater signal for epidemic early warning and emergency response, and inflow-side data for digital twins of sewer and treatment systems. Related records: WastewaterSCAN (data-wastewaterscan) and Germany's AMELAG (data-rki-amelag-wastewater-surveillance).
licence: Public Domain (US Government); WastewaterSCAN rows CC BY-NC 4.0
